:::{#thm-qr}
#### QR factorization

Let $\matr{A}$ be an $m \times n$ matrix with $\operatorname{rank}(\matr{A}) = n$.
Then

$$
\underbrace{\matr{A}}_{m \times n} = \underbrace{\matr{Q}}_{m \times n}\,\underbrace{\matr{R}}_{n \times n},
$$

where the columns of $\matr{Q}$ are orthonormal (@def-orthonormal-vectors)
and $\matr{R}$ is upper triangular (@def-triangular-matrix) with positive diagonal entries.

:::

::: proof

The $n$ columns $\vecf{a}_1, \ldots, \vecf{a}_n$ of $\matr{A}$ are linearly independent
(@def-full-column-rank),
so the Gram-Schmidt process (@def-gram-schmidt) runs all $n$ steps
and gives orthonormal $\vecf{q}_1, \ldots, \vecf{q}_n$ (@thm-gram-schmidt, parts 1 and 3);
let $\matr{Q}$ have these columns.
At step $i$, $\tilde{\vecf{q}}_i \ne \vzero$, and rearranging the orthogonalize step,

$$
\ba
\vecf{a}_i
&= \tilde{\vecf{q}}_i + \sum_{j=1}^{i-1} (\vecf{q}_j \cdot \vecf{a}_i)\,\vecf{q}_j
&& \text{(add the sum to both sides of the orthogonalize step)}
\\
&= \norm{\tilde{\vecf{q}}_i}\,\vecf{q}_i + \sum_{j=1}^{i-1} (\vecf{q}_j \cdot \vecf{a}_i)\,\vecf{q}_j.
&& \text{(normalize step: } \tilde{\vecf{q}}_i = \norm{\tilde{\vecf{q}}_i}\,\vecf{q}_i \text{)}
\ea
$$

Let $\matr{R}$ be the $n \times n$ matrix with
$r_{ji} = \vecf{q}_j \cdot \vecf{a}_i$ for $j < i$,
$r_{ii} = \norm{\tilde{\vecf{q}}_i} > 0$,
and $r_{ji} = 0$ for $j > i$;
it is upper triangular with positive diagonal.
Column $i$ of $\matr{Q} \matr{R}$ is $\matr{Q}$ times column $i$ of $\matr{R}$ (@def-matrix-mult), and

$$
\ba
\matr{Q}\,(r_{1i}, \ldots, r_{ni})
&= \sum_{j=1}^{n} r_{ji}\,\vecf{q}_j
&& \text{(@thm-matvec-columns)}
\\
&= \sum_{j=1}^{i} r_{ji}\,\vecf{q}_j
&& \text{(} r_{ji} = 0 \text{ for } j > i \text{)}
\\
&= r_{ii}\,\vecf{q}_i + \sum_{j=1}^{i-1} r_{ji}\,\vecf{q}_j
&& \text{(split off the } j = i \text{ term)}
\\
&= \vecf{a}_i.
&& \text{(the entries of } \matr{R} \text{, and the display)}
\ea
$$

So $\matr{Q} \matr{R} = \matr{A}$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-qr}
#### A QR factorization from Gram-Schmidt

For $\matr{A}$ with columns $\vecf{a}_1 = (1, 1, 0)$, $\vecf{a}_2 = (1, 0, 1)$, $\vecf{a}_3 = (0, 1, 1)$,
@exm-gram-schmidt and @exm-thm-gram-schmidt found
$\vecf{q}_1 = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\,(1, 1, 0)$,
$\vecf{q}_2 = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\,(1, -1, 2)$,
$\vecf{q}_3 = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\,(-1, 1, 1)$,
with $\norm{\tilde{\vecf{q}}_1} = \sqrt{2}$, $\norm{\tilde{\vecf{q}}_2} = \sqrt{3/2}$,
$\norm{\tilde{\vecf{q}}_3} = 2/\sqrt{3}$,
$\vecf{q}_1 \cdot \vecf{a}_2 = \vecf{q}_1 \cdot \vecf{a}_3 = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
and $\vecf{q}_2 \cdot \vecf{a}_3 = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}$. So

$$
\matr{R} = \begin{bmatrix}
\sqrt{2} & \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\
0 & \sqrt{3/2} & \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \\
0 & 0 & \tfrac{2}{\sqrt{3}}
\end{bmatrix}.
$$

As a check on the second column,
$\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\,\vecf{q}_1 + \sqrt{3/2}\,\vecf{q}_2
= \tfrac{1}{2}\,(1, 1, 0) + \tfrac{1}{2}\,(1, -1, 2) = (1, 0, 1) = \vecf{a}_2$.

:::
